claim: *Composition by reference.* Stable identities join the user-journey, service, coverage, test-placement, and execution-policy views. The resulting joined view supports cross-model queries without duplicating those facts into a single stored model.
topology:
A cross-model question is answered by joining small, question-specific views on stable
    identities. A user journey, carrying goal and criticality, joins to a service or node along a dashed
    endpoint-identity arrow. From that service, three dashed arrows fan out to sibling views: a coverage view
    asking whether it is exercised, a test-placement view asking where it runs, and an execution-policy view
    that plans for the host. The three sibling views then converge, along dashed arrows, on a joined view
    labelled not a mega-model. Every join edge is dashed: these are derived correspondences across views, and no
    fact is copied into a single stored model. No heavy boundary appears — composition is correspondence, not
    enforcement. Legend as in Figure C-1; dash and weight carry the meaning without colour.
required_terms: Dashed: derived correspondence on stable identities; no copied facts.
bw_encoding: Ordinary nodes, artifacts, evidence and outcomes are white. Named roles, position and relation styles provide the necessary distinctions.
redesign: Layout reflowed for a 15 cm monochrome print column; color categories replaced by labels and boundary weight.
alt: Composition by reference — join small views on stable identities, not one mega-model
